Private Dejan Milosevic, to the best of your recollection, was he involved in this blockade at all during those four days?

utterances.speaker: PAVLE GAVRILOVIC
utterances.text: He certainly wasn't; I've already said that. Private Dejan Milosevic, I remember him, I have an excellent recollection of him, he is a soldier from Pristina, and he had a hip problem, due to which he could not walk properly. So he was partially unfit for military service. He worked in a workshop. He certainly didn't do anything there.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: In your battalion did you have another person by the name of Dejan Milosevic?

utterances.speaker: PAVLE GAVRILOVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Mr. Gavrilovic, or rather, this same witness with respect to this same action, talking about their descent into the village of Trnje, he says that the members of your battalion threw hand-grenades into houses. The members of the logistics battalion, did they have hand-grenades at all?

utterances.speaker: PAVLE GAVRILOVIC
utterances.text: They did not have hand-grenades; that is to say that was impossible that any one of these men had them.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Are you talking about this action or are you talking about this in general throughout the war?

utterances.speaker: PAVLE GAVRILOVIC
utterances.text: I'm saying in general. Soldiers did not have hand-grenades. It is impossible that any one of them had them.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Mr. Gavrilovic, could we please have a look at P1995. I have the second page of this document in B/C/S. Mr. Gavrilovic, under paragraph 2 in the first subparagraph and in the first bullet point we see BG-1 and further on. It says: "VJ forces were engaged." Is the logistics battalion included in the engaged forces there or part of the logistics battalion for that matter?

utterances.speaker: PAVLE GAVRILOVIC
utterances.text: No, no, the logistics battalion is not there or not even part of it. Simply because we were not the engaged forces, we were the blockade forces.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Now let us have a look, perhaps it will be easier for us to have a look from the bottom of the page, the first, second, third, fourth paragraph, and the last sentence there. Could you read it out and could you tell us whether these forces in the blockade refer to your unit or to part of your unit?

utterances.speaker: MS. CARTER
utterances.text: Can I get a page reference in the English, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Mr. Bakrac.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] In English it is the next page, Your Honours, page 3 -- no, sorry, 4. If I may assist my colleague, in English it's towards the bottom of the page, it's a bit lower than this. It is the last sentence. I am sorry. Let me just have a look. I guess it's on page 5, as a matter of fact. It starts with the following words: "During the course of the third day ..." Yes. Your Honour -- well, yes, for the Court and for my colleague it is the second paragraph, the first, second, third, fourth, fifth line, that's where it says: "The villages of Trnje and Lesane, the forces under the blockade ..." We can go back to the B/C/S version. I hope that I have assisted the Trial Chamber and my colleague.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Could you please read the last sentence?

utterances.speaker: PAVLE GAVRILOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: And tell us, does this refer to your part of the unit?

utterances.speaker: PAVLE GAVRILOVIC
utterances.text: "The forces under the blockade along the asphalt road and in the area of Siroko, Smac, and Donja Srbica were still in their positions." This precisely refers to the part of the unit that was there.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Did you have any movements during these four days?

utterances.speaker: PAVLE GAVRILOVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Mr. Gavrilovic, Witness (redacted) said that part of your battalion, or rather, that, or rather, that part of your battalion did find a local Albanian in the area of deployment of the technical company of that battalion and that he was interviewed and then executed, shot. Can you remember any such incident?

utterances.speaker: PAVLE GAVRILOVIC
utterances.text: I can exactly remember this particular incident because it was just that one and only incident. It was the only such person found in the area of deployment of my unit and in general.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Let us now look at 5D228, that's a combat report of --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Is that all that's to be asked on that?

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: You're still on the same subject. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honour, of course. I'd like us to have a look at this and then I'm going to put two or three other questions in relation to that.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Look at 1.2: "Activities of the STS" and then we have paragraph 2. Could you read this second paragraph, or rather, subparagraph: "Guards of the support battalion, or rather, logistics battalion ..."

utterances.speaker: PAVLE GAVRILOVIC
utterances.text: This precisely pertains to that. This is what it says: "Guards of the logistics battalion of the 549th Motorised Brigade" --

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Do slow down.

utterances.speaker: PAVLE GAVRILOVIC
utterances.text: " ... captured terrorist Gashi Shukri who was under cover around the redeployment area of the unit. Before that he discarded an automatic rifle with three clips of ammunition and a knife marked KLA. He confessed to being a member of the KLA terrorist organization. He is being processed by the security organ and the military police."

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Mr. Gavrilovic --

utterances.speaker: MS. CARTER
utterances.text: Respectfully, Your Honour, I'm wondering if there's a translation issue. 5D228 is in regards to combat operations that took place on 22 May of 1999. It's my understanding that we were discussing March of 1999. So either there's a translation problem, or I'm not clear how these two items are related.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Mr. Bakrac.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I don't know. I didn't manage to follow these documents and the translation, we're not talking about March at all. I asked about the war period, and now I'm going to ask him further about the war period, whether there were other such incidents. I wasn't talking about March.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: You were talking about a specific allegation made by (redacted). Now, what period did that relate to?

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, the war period, and in the statement of this witness there is no time specified. He says: "One day somebody was shooting at the army, and as a consequence of that we found ..." "As a consequence of that we found a local Albanian. I'm sure that he wasn't the one shooting at us, but he was interviewed and executed."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Mr. Gavrilovic, the person you have just referred to as having been arrested, how did he die?

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, may --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Just a moment.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This person -- well, I don't know whether he lost his life or not, but he certainly wasn't executed by a firing squad or something like that. He was handed over to the organs of the military police, and as far as I know, charges were brought against this person.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Do you know that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [No verbal response]

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: What were the charges?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I don't know the exact details now, but I do now how this incident occurred, I remember that, because it was characteristic case. With your permission I may explain.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: No, I would just like to know what happened afterwards, but you don't know anything about the proceedings that were taken against him?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I know of the proceedings -- this is the procedure. This person was handed over to the organs of the military police --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: But do you know what actually happened to him after that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I don't know. I know that criminal charges were brought against him and now later whether he was convicted or not --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: What were the criminal charges then if you know about them?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, you see, this is the way it was. This person had weapons on him, a rifle and ammunition and a knife that was found on the site where the person himself was found, so --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: You've told us all that. Just tell me if you know what the criminal charges were. They're in a document normally. Now, do you know what this document charging him -- or do you even know that there was a document on which he was charged before a military court?

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I saw this kind of document when I spoke to the lawyer, Mr. Bakrac, that's why I know it exists, but ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: In relation to this particular person?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, precisely in relation to that person.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: What's his name?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Gashi, Shukri Gashi.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Bakrac.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Mr. Gavrilovic, can we now have a look at 5D903, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I would like to draw the attention of the honourable Trial Chamber to the fact that in this combat report of the command of the Pristina Corps that we looked at a few moments ago, because we cannot have both documents on the screen at the same time, in the combat report it says: "Shukri Gashi, son of Dervish," that is what is included in that report; the father's name is included as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Is this a criminal report from the 22nd of May, 1999, and also the combat report pertains to the 22nd of May, 1999, criminal report, filed to the military prosecutor against Shukri Gashi, father's name Dervish?

utterances.speaker: PAVLE GAVRILOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. That is precisely the criminal report.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: To move along faster, does it say in the criminal report that the authorised officer of the military police says: "When I was taking over Gashi Shukri, I told Sergeant first class Ljubisa Stojanovic to search the place where the detainee who was arrested at sunrise." Who is this sergeant first class Sergeant Stojanovic?

utterances.speaker: PAVLE GAVRILOVIC
utterances.text: He was a squad commander and on that day he was the duty officer. As for Shukri Gashi, he was stopped by security guards near the technical school where this unit was stationed at 2 after midnight.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: So if I understood you correctly, he was not executed; he was turned over to the military police and later to the military prosecution office?

utterances.speaker: PAVLE GAVRILOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, correct. I don't know whether he was convicted or not.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Apart from this incident involving this person, was there any member of your logistical platoon who had occasion to arrest a KLA member or a civilian?

utterances.speaker: PAVLE GAVRILOVIC
utterances.text: No, no.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Mr. Bakrac, do you also have documents to show what happened as the result of this report?

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, not for the time being. I have charged someone with reviewing whether there are any documents in the files for terrorist activity and related charges. I expect to find out what the further procedure was like.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Mr. Gavrilovic, I have just one more question, and that is -- it has to do with you. (redacted)

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: (redacted) We talked, and as far as I understood there was a plan to drive out Albanian civilians from Kosovo." First of all, it says "during NATO air-strikes." During NATO air-strikes before and after the war, who was your driver?

utterances.speaker: PAVLE GAVRILOVIC
utterances.text: That soldier, (redacted) whatever, certainly wasn't my driver. My driver was recruit Goran Stefanovic, a man from around Leskovac who still lives there. So it was certainly not that soldier.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Did (redacted) ever drive your car?

utterances.speaker: PAVLE GAVRILOVIC
utterances.text: No, certainly not.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, those were all my questions for this witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Bakrac. Mr. Ackerman.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: Mr. Gavrilovic, I just have a question or two. I'm John Ackerman; I represent General Pavkovic. At the beginning of your testimony you talked about the village of Damjane --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Can we, by the way, go into open session for your cross-examination or --

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: Sure.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: -- is that dangerous?

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: I don't think it's dangerous at all.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Very well. Let's go into open session now.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We are in open session, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Please continue, Mr. Ackerman.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: During your examination you talked about this village Damjane and you mentioned there was civilians there who remained there. First of all, do you have any idea the number of civilians that were in that village, how many?

utterances.speaker: PAVLE GAVRILOVIC
utterances.text: I cannot tell you the exact number of civilians now, but it's a normal village.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: About how many houses would you say are in the village?

utterances.speaker: PAVLE GAVRILOVIC
utterances.text: I really cannot tell you how many houses there were, but certainly around 50, maybe more, because I practically didn't go into the village when I toured part of my unit because my unit was in the broader area of that village, not inside.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: Do you know if those civilians remained in that village throughout the entire 78 days of the NATO campaign or do you not know that?

utterances.speaker: PAVLE GAVRILOVIC
utterances.text: I don't know that. I think they did, they did stay.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: Was there any NATO bombing that you know of that village or any NATO bombing in the vicinity of that village?

utterances.speaker: PAVLE GAVRILOVIC
utterances.text: I really couldn't tell you now. I don't remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: All right. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Now, Mr. Bakrac, we're about, obviously, to have cross-examination from the Prosecutor; that raises the possibility I think that you will reach another witness in the course of today, and I see concern has been expressed about the short notice given of the statement of the next witness that you propose to lead. Are you going to alter the order of witnesses?

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I dealt with the three previous and two current ones, a total of five; my colleague, Mr. Cepic, should handle the next four, and I believe he had problems with getting translations from the CLSS. He knows more about it because he communicated with the CLSS. I'm not sure if he's ready to report, but I'll ask my helper to call Mr. Cepic to clarify this and to inform you because he will do that better. But I believe the order of witnesses has not been altered. I believe it's the same one that was announced by the case manager to the Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Mr. Hannis.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Your Honour, in addition to what I raised regarding the timing, in going through the statement this morning I discovered that the first 20 paragraphs, the English translation is quite --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: It's incomprehensible.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Yes, yes. After that it seems to be translated by someone else and that's much more understandable, but I would request a further translation of those first 20 paragraphs because otherwise I can't deal with it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: But as far as the timing is concerned, your position is that you will not be in a position to deal with him until Wednesday; is that right?

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Well, yes, Your Honour, but I don't want to force myself by my own petard by moving him to later and then having Vukovic advance, for example, who is in my estimation a more significant witness who I would rather have some additional time to prepare for. So if I don't have to start my cross-examination of this witness until tomorrow afternoon, I'll probably be ready to do it if we can do something about the first 20 paragraphs.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Mr. Bakrac, who translated the first part of the statement? Or do you not know?

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'm in the in a position to tell you now, Your Honour, because Mr. Cepic was looking for possibilities over the weekend because he found out from the CLSS on Friday that they cannot manage a translation by then. I was working in the meantime with the current witnesses. I have to find out from him or bring him here to inform you.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: The concern I have about that, Your Honour, is the statement was taken on the 27th and 28th of December.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Yeah, well that's what makes it odd, yes, I agree. It's not one of these statements prepared at the last minute. Mr. Cepic will have to be here later today should we get to the stage of possibly calling that witness, and he should also be asked meanwhile to explore the possibility of advancing someone else but that would be someone other than Vukovic. Now, we will continue with the examination. You will now be cross-examined by the Prosecutor, Ms. Carter. Ms. Carter.

utterances.speaker: MS. CARTER
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MS. CARTER
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Lieutenant-Colonel. My name is April Carter, and I am here on behalf of the Office of the Prosecution and I have some questions for you with regards to the operations your units were engaged in in 1999. The first thing that I would like to do is call up P3078.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The Prosecutor is kindly asked to slow down. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. CARTER
utterances.text: Sir, the primary feature in your statement is the operation that took place on or about 24 March of 1999 on your place near the village of Trnje. I am showing you a map of those villages, and I would ask the court to draw down to the very middle sector just to the left of Suva Reka, which is where the engagement took place. Sir, do you see the village of Trnje?

utterances.speaker: PAVLE GAVRILOVIC
utterances.text: [In English] I don't see -- [Interpretation] I don't.

utterances.speaker: MS. CARTER
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: PAVLE GAVRILOVIC
utterances.text: It's not clear at all.

utterances.speaker: MS. CARTER
utterances.text: Do you see the village of Prizren to the bottom of the screen?

utterances.speaker: PAVLE GAVRILOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. CARTER
utterances.text: Okay. If you look to the line, the straight grid line to its right and go immediately up to the second graphic you should be able to see it almost right on that line. Do you see it now?

utterances.speaker: PAVLE GAVRILOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. CARTER
utterances.text: Perhaps we can further blow up that portion of the map. Okay. And a little further. All right.

utterances.speaker: MS. CARTER
utterances.text: And now the Trnje village is actually to the far right-hand of the screen. Do you still see it, in the middle sector?

utterances.speaker: PAVLE GAVRILOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. CARTER
utterances.text: Okay. In paragraph 8 of your statement, you indicate that 30 of your men took a position on that hill on 25 March of 1999; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: PAVLE GAVRILOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. CARTER
utterances.text: And specifically, that hill was between Mamusa and Trnje, and that's about 500 metres off Trnje; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: PAVLE GAVRILOVIC
utterances.text: Correct, 500 to 1.000 metres.

utterances.speaker: MS. CARTER
utterances.text: And for ease of reference if we can have the witness mark exactly where those 30 men were deployed on the map.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, I cannot mark it exactly on the map, but roughly it's around here.

utterances.speaker: MS. CARTER
utterances.text: All right. And if you could mark that with an A, please.

utterances.speaker: PAVLE GAVRILOVIC
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MS. CARTER
utterances.text: Now, you've indicated to the Court that the blockade lasted four days and your people never moved off that position; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: PAVLE GAVRILOVIC
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. CARTER
utterances.text: What was your line of sight like between your position and the village of Trnje?

utterances.speaker: PAVLE GAVRILOVIC
utterances.text: I emphasised in my statement that the weather was very bad, and from the place where we were, we were able to see only a couple of houses, two or three houses.

utterances.speaker: MS. CARTER
utterances.text: So outside of the weather itself, there was nothing to block your line of sight between your position and Trnje village; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: PAVLE GAVRILOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, we were on the hill.

utterances.speaker: MS. CARTER
utterances.text: Now, you've indicated in your statement that you did not see or hear any movement within Trnje village; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: PAVLE GAVRILOVIC
utterances.text: I didn't quite understand. In what sense I did not see?

utterances.speaker: MS. CARTER
utterances.text: In paragraph 12 of your statement you specifically state that: "I did not observe any movement or combat in the village." Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: PAVLE GAVRILOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. CARTER
utterances.text: And is that true for all four days that you were deployed on that hilltop?

utterances.speaker: PAVLE GAVRILOVIC
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. CARTER
utterances.text: Now -- but you have indicated that you did hear combat operations in surrounding areas. Can you please identify for the Court which positions that you do believe combat took place over those four days.

utterances.speaker: PAVLE GAVRILOVIC
utterances.text: When I gave that statement, I didn't mean specific positions because it's impossible to determine the exact position. We heard sporadic fire. I don't know from which direction it came. I cannot determine from here or from there. I didn't see anyone shooting, so I cannot tell you from where the fire came, but gun-fire was heard.

utterances.speaker: MS. CARTER
utterances.text: The gun-fire that you did hear, do you believe that it was further away from you than where Trnje village featured?

utterances.speaker: PAVLE GAVRILOVIC
utterances.text: Roughly, yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. CARTER
utterances.text: That's all I'll need off this exhibit, if I can have an IC number, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: That will be IC173, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. CARTER
utterances.text: I'd now like to call up P1995 and looking at page 5 in the English, the first full paragraph, and page 2, the fourth paragraph from the bottom in the B/C/S.

utterances.speaker: MS. CARTER
utterances.text: Sir, the reason I was asking you questions about where you were located as well as where there was combat operations is because you've indicated that while you were on that hill you were not seeing anything in Trnje, yet if you look to the fourth paragraph from the bottom where you had cited that: "The forces under the blockade line along the asphalt road in the area of Siroko, Smac, and Donja Srbica were still in their positions." I would actually direct you just above to where it says: "A part of the STS forces attempted to pull out along the creek to the villages of Trnje and Lesane," and then going down further to the fourth day operations, it indicates that: "Over that night, the STS, they had pulled out of the villages of Trnje and Lesane during the night were also routed and crushed." What I'm asking you is: How did you miss the fact that there was clearly an operation occurring in Trnje village pursuant to the combat report that you yourself cited in your statement?

utterances.speaker: PAVLE GAVRILOVIC
utterances.text: I have already said at the beginning that I was able to see only two or three houses of that village from where I was. The village itself was in a depression. I was able to see two or three houses only, so I didn't misspeak. I just heard gun-fire. I couldn't determine whether it was from left to the village, from right to the village, from behind, or from where.

utterances.speaker: MS. CARTER
utterances.text: But, sir, from paragraph 12 in your statement you indicate that you did not observe any movement or combat in the village. So again I ask you, how do you explain that in your statement you're placing no combat activity whatsoever in that village, yet there very clearly was an operation over the night of the third day going into the fourth morning 500 metres from you?

utterances.speaker: PAVLE GAVRILOVIC
utterances.text: You see, I did not see that operation that you are referring to and I didn't participate in it and my part of the unit did not take part in it. That's what I meant when I said that in the statement. I don't know which passage from my statement that you're referring to.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, may I propose that the usher hand a copy of Mr. Gavrilovic's statement to the witness so he can follow.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Certainly. Ms. Carter.

utterances.speaker: MS. CARTER
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MS. CARTER
utterances.text: Sir, if you can just read through paragraph 12 of your statement and then I'll further ask some questions about it. Once you've finished reading it, if you can let me know.

utterances.speaker: PAVLE GAVRILOVIC
utterances.text: "Since it was the end of winter and the beginning of spring, the weather was cold and foggy all the four days and we were barely able to glimpse" --

utterances.speaker: MS. CARTER
utterances.text: Sir, we can all read paragraph 12 of your statement. What I'm more concerned about is that again you note: "I did not observe any movement or combat in the village." The sentence does go on: "But we did hear the place where we were located that there was combat in the wide sector" --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Slow down when reading, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. CARTER
utterances.text: "There was combat in the wide sector ahead of us in the course of those four days." I asked you previously when marking the map if the operations that you did hear were within Trnje or if they were in further placements. You indicated that they were actually further than Trnje village. I'm asking you now for a third time: How does that correspond with P1995 that says there was, in fact, an operation ongoing 500 metres from you in Trnje village? Are you now conceding that there was, in fact, an operation going on there and that you did, in fact, observe it?

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Just a moment. Mr. Bakrac, just please let this question be answered.

utterances.speaker: MS. CARTER
utterances.text: Will you please answer my question.

utterances.speaker: PAVLE GAVRILOVIC
utterances.text: I did not understand the question, but if the question was -- I wrote clearly that I had not observed any movement or combat from my position, because from where I was, I couldn't see the village. But it was audible in the broader area around us, so I cannot determine whether it was from a distance of 1 kilometre on my right or 500 metres on my left. I already explained. Sporadic gun-fire was heard throughout the four days, not only during the night.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Mr. Bakrac.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I would appreciate a reference from Ms. Carter that combat was going on. Where it says part of the STS tried along the brook to pull out towards Lesane and Trnje, it doesn't say that combat was going on there. It says "had pulled out into the villages of Trnje and Lesane." I would just like a reference.

utterances.speaker: MS. CARTER
utterances.text: I would invite counsel to look at the following paragraph that speaks to: "In the course of the fourth day," the final sentence in which: "The STS had pulled out into the villages of Trnje and Lesane during the night were also routed and crushed."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Is that good enough, Mr. Bakrac?

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honour, but attention was drawn to the third day and the withdrawal, and here we see when it is happening, the fourth day, and at what time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: The question related to the whole period. Please continue, Ms. Carter.

utterances.speaker: MS. CARTER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. CARTER
utterances.text: Lieutenant-Colonel, I would direct your attention to the answer that you actually had given previously on page 66 of today's transcript when we were going over where combat operations were actually taking place. You had indicated that you could not be specific, but the question I finally asked you is that the gun-fire that you did hear, do you believe that was further away from you than where Trnje village featured and you indicated roughly, yes. Throughout that entire exchange you held on to the position that nothing occurred in Trnje village. And I want to know from you, given that P1995 indicates that terrorists were being routed and crushed 500 metres from you: Either, 1, were you not that observant; or 2, were you telling the Court an inaccuracy?

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: Your Honour --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Mr. --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I did not say anything to the Court about --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Hold on. Mr. Ackerman.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: Your Honour, I maybe shouldn't have stood up, but the -- I think the questions are decidedly unfair --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: I think we can judge when we read them in light of what's been said and what answer is given; but I don't think -- they may be difficult but they're not, on the face of it, unfair.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: Well, Your Honour, she's taken the position that the forces were in the village of Trnje and Lesane and action took place there, and that paragraph about the third day says they attempted to pull out along the creek to those villages but it never says that they actually went to those villages, that they just attempted to go there. And attempted to go there probably means they didn't ever make it. So for her to suggest that there was a battle going on in those villages is just not supported by this document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: The fourth paragraph, last sentence, rather undermines that proposition I think, and it is a matter of interpretation in the end of the day for us to deal with. Mr. Zecevic.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Well, Your Honours, actually Mr. Ackerman is right. The translation of this document is not good. It doesn't --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: I don't think that's what he was saying, Mr. Zecevic.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: I'm sorry?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: I don't think that's what he's saying.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Well, my understanding of the -- of the -- of the paragraph referring to the fourth day, it does -- the Serbian text is different from the actual English translation.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Mr. --

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Maybe --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: -- Gavrilovic, would you look at the paragraph dealing with the fourth day and would you read the last sentence, that's the last sentence only of that paragraph, and read it out to us.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] "Also, the Siptar terrorist forces that had pulled out into the villages of Trnje and Lesane under the cover of the night were routed and crushed."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Is that wrong, Mr. Zecevic?

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Well, it would -- the way how it's translated, Your Honour, it would suggest that there was a clash, and that they were routed and crushed in the vicinity of these villages; but that is not what the Serbian text says. The Serbian text says they were routed and crushed and then they pulled out towards the villages of Trnje and Lesane. So --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: But you can't -- I mean, that's rather illogical.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: I don't know why? They're informing in this combat report that there has been a clash with the terrorist forces. They were routed and crushed, and then they pulled out; the terrorist forces pulled out towards the village of Trnje and Lesane. That is what it says in the Serbian text. I mean, I -- I don't want to really put the pressure on the interpreters or anything, but I -- that is at least my understanding of the Serbian. I don't know if I'm correctly expressing myself in English, but that's the gist of it. Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Well, we'll try one final time in light of your comments, Mr. Zecevic. Could you please, Mr. Gavrilovic, read aloud that sentence again.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Only the last sentence? "Also what was carried out was the crushing and destroying of the Siptar terrorist forces, STS, which under the cover of night got out into the village of Trnje and Lesane."

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's note: A very literal translation.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Well, Ms. Carter, I doubt if there's any more to be gained by further cross-examination on this particular point, and we shall ask CLSS for a formal retranslation of that whole paragraph beginning: "In the course of the fourth day ..."

utterances.speaker: MS. CARTER
utterances.text: Certainly, Your Honour. And the next topic I would like to cover needs to be taken in private session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Very well. We shall go into private session.

utterances.speaker: MS. CARTER
utterances.text: Sir, you have -- 19 [Private session] [Confidentiality lifted by later order of the Chamber]

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We are in private session, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MS. CARTER
utterances.text: Sir, throughout your statement you have indicated that (redacted) (redacted)were mistaken in their arguments that they were actually involved in operations in and near Trnje village; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: PAVLE GAVRILOVIC
utterances.text: I didn't understand what it was that you asked me. What was the mistake? What was this mistake that was made?

utterances.speaker: MS. CARTER
utterances.text: No. I'm asking you -- you've indicated in our previous conversation that you were always on the hilltop, and while there may or may not have been anything going on near Trnje village, you were indicating that none of your men were involved in any sort of activity outside of standing guard on that hilltop; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: PAVLE GAVRILOVIC
utterances.text: That is absolutely correct. However, I didn't understand the last point --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The interpreter did not hear the witness to the end. Could other microphones please be switched off while he is speaking. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I don't know what the question refers to.

utterances.speaker: MS. CARTER
utterances.text: I'm simply trying to confirm that it seems that there may have been a mistaken with regards to what was going on in Trnje village. I'm just trying to determine how far that mistake may have gone. You are now saying that there may have been something going in -- in or near Trnje, but your units most certainly were not involved in it. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: PAVLE GAVRILOVIC
utterances.text: As I've already said, my soldiers did not participate in anything; that is to say we were going downhill. Now, whether something was going on in the village or not, I really don't know about that because I was at a relatively far away distance; and I saw only two or three houses in the village from the position where I was.

utterances.speaker: MS. CARTER
utterances.text: Sir, you have had the opportunity to read the statement of (redacted) and you were commenting on it within your own statement; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: PAVLE GAVRILOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. CARTER
utterances.text: Within that statement, which is (redacted)

utterances.speaker: MS. CARTER
utterances.text: (redacted)in which some MUP reports were provided, they were P2305 and P2304, they are a part of that statement. Sir, both (redacted) as well as the exhibits P2305 and P2304 place four civilians being shot at that same creek bed about 500 metres from Trnje in the direction of Mamusa, which is directly on your position. Can you please explain how both (redacted) as well as the MUP were able to determine that civilians were being killed near Trnje in your area of operation, yet you believe none of your men were involved.

utterances.speaker: PAVLE GAVRILOVIC
utterances.text: If I understood you correctly, you said towards Mamusa, that is to the left, that is not towards Trnje. But certainly no one participated, none of the men that I was with there.

utterances.speaker: MS. CARTER
utterances.text: Sir, to be specific, the bodies were found 500 to 800 metres from Trnje in the direction of Mamusa, where you have described in paragraph 9 that the hill in which you were placed was between Mamusa and Trnje about 500 metres until you get to Trnje. It's the exact same place or within a couple of hundred metres. Can you please explain if not your people, as (redacted) alleges, then who were killing the civilians that the MUP found and provided reports on?

utterances.speaker: PAVLE GAVRILOVIC
utterances.text: I really don't know what civilians this is about. If we understand each other correctly, you're referring to a creek, and I'm saying that part of my unit was up on a hill that's far away. In front of me there was a big meadow and then there was a brook or a creek in that field, so it's very far away from the place where I was with my men. I really don't know who could have ...

utterances.speaker: MS. CARTER
utterances.text: Can we bring back the IC exhibit number --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: 137, is it?

utterances.speaker: MS. CARTER
utterances.text: -- 137, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Sorry, yes, 173.

utterances.speaker: MS. CARTER
utterances.text: Sir, throughout this area where your hilltop is, there are any number of creeks and streams. And (redacted) was quite specific where he had indicated that he was deployed, and he was actually a part of the group who eventually killed a number of civilians on that spot. If you could see Trnje or at least a few houses of it, how is it you were able to miss the creek beds?

utterances.speaker: PAVLE GAVRILOVIC
utterances.text: Are you understanding me right? I said that there was a field or meadow in front of me and that there was a creek or brook in the middle of that field. I'm not saying that I did not see a creek at all.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Ms. Carter, is this a convenient time to interrupt you?

utterances.speaker: MS. CARTER
utterances.text: Certainly, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Mr. Gavrilovic, we interrupt now for a break for an hour. Could you please leave the courtroom with the usher.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I do apologise. I'm trying to be -- I'm trying to be useful. I don't know English very well, but on page 74, line 19, please take a look at it at the break. I think that the answer is not there. I think that the interpreters said that they didn't understand him. If this is important, well and fine; if it's not, then I apologise for taking up your time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: I think the witness went on to deal with it, Mr. Fila, when he said: "I don't know what the question refers to," and then Ms. Carter asked it again. So I don't know any harm has been done in the end of the day. Thank you. We shall resume at 1.45. --- Luncheon recess taken at 12.47 p.m.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Ms. Carter.

utterances.speaker: MS. CARTER
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MS. CARTER
utterances.text: Sir, when you were testifying on direct examination it appeared that you were saying that the logistics battalion at all times was only involved in supporting the units and was never involved in any sort of combat operations. Is that a correct understanding of your evidence?

utterances.speaker: PAVLE GAVRILOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. CARTER
utterances.text: And is this a true statement throughout the war time?

utterances.speaker: PAVLE GAVRILOVIC
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: MS. CARTER
utterances.text: I'd like to bring up P3081, which was Milosevic Exhibit 925, it's the war diary of the 549th, it's going to be page 115 in the English and page 167 in the B/C/S.

utterances.speaker: MS. CARTER
utterances.text: Sir, within your units did you have a man by the name of Sergeant First Class Fezik?

utterances.speaker: PAVLE GAVRILOVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. CARTER
utterances.text: Was there another logistics battalion for the 549th?

utterances.speaker: PAVLE GAVRILOVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. CARTER
utterances.text: I would direct you to the assignment, this is from May 29th of 1999, where it's indicating an assignment for the logistics battalion. And in fact it goes on to say that: "30 soldiers were sent on an assignment in the area around," an illegible word, "that was the Prizren military department in battle with the STS with members of the MUP and the VJ and seven terrorists were killed." Can you tell me then how you differentiate this assignment for the logistics battalion if they're in operations and seven people are getting killed, how is that not a combat operation?

utterances.speaker: PAVLE GAVRILOVIC
utterances.text: In my statement I already wrote and said that we directly took part -- we did not take part in any combat operations directly -- well, a few times we did, part of the unit, as I wrote in my statement; and in this case about 30 men who were used only to prevent spillovers of terrorists, or rather, to get them out of their positions. As for this particular mission, I don't know what this is about exactly. It says Fejzic here, Sergeant Fejzic, he was indeed a member of the logistics battalion, whereas I heard a different name, Fe something in the interpretation.

utterances.speaker: MS. CARTER
utterances.text: But, sir, my very first question to you was that when you were testifying on direct examination it appeared that you were saying that the logistics battalion at all times was only involved in supporting the units and was never involved in any sort of combat operations and you said --

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: Your Honour --

utterances.speaker: MS. CARTER
utterances.text: -- Yes, yes --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: I rise again to protest fairness. If you look at the document it's so clear that first of all you have logistics battalion: And describes what it wants to describe with regards to logistics battalion, which ends with 30 men being sent on an assignment, doesn't say combat assignment, doesn't say to attack anybody. And then the next section deals with the Prizren military department, where there's a colon, and describes what they did which has to do with what she's trying to lay on this logistics battalion. Just anybody could read that and figure out that that's what it's about. It's very clear.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Ms. Carter.

utterances.speaker: MS. CARTER
utterances.text: That interpretation is available; however, the witness at page 79, starting at line 1 specifically says: "In my statement I already wrote and said that we directly took part -- we did not take part in the combat operations directly. Well, a few times we did a part of the unit, as I wrote in the statement." There becomes a discrepancy because the witness very clearly on direct examination and at the beginning of this examination was quick to remove himself and any portion of his unit from combat operations, yet he's already conceding at page 79 that he in fact was, or at least portions of it were part of combat operations, and I'd like to explore that topic. So while interpretation may be wrong, I think that we stumbled across the truth one way or another.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Just one moment. You spent considerable time examining the witnesses about the part the unit played in the blockade at Trnje.

utterances.speaker: MS. CARTER
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour; however, this is actually moving on more to the May period --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Yes, but you can't possibly interpret his evidence as being to the effect that they never participated in any form of combat.

utterances.speaker: MS. CARTER
utterances.text: Your Honour, during direct examination -- and actually at page 79 starting at line 1 that is what he went on to say -- this unit only provide the logistics, I think there was one comment at the very beginning of his testimony --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Yes, I've got that, but you're telling us that in direct examination he said that they did not participate in any way in combat, and that's not right. This statement is part of his direct examination.

utterances.speaker: MS. CARTER
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour but what they always say that they were only a part of the blockade line in fact it went on -- I think it went on with regards to a water truck, did you ever see a water truck in the beginning. So there was always the impression given that the only thing this unit was doing was either providing a blockade line or providing support to the units that were in combat, and that's why I began asking at page 79 --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Being part of a blockade is obviously involvement in some capacity in a combat operation; however, the particular point that's being made here is that what you presented was a misrepresentation of the war diary. Now, I take it you accept that?

utterances.speaker: MS. CARTER
utterances.text: I believe they're -- when I was originally reading it to be quite frank, Your Honour, I didn't -- the semi-colon was lost upon me on the second -- so it is conceivable that Mr. Ackerman's assessment of this is correct. However, I would rely on line 79 -- sorry page 79, at line 1, to begin asking questions about the combat -- direct involvement --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Well, there is no objection to you asking these questions. The only objection is to you characterizing the entry in the war diary as indicative of combat. So please proceed but without reference to the war diary.

utterances.speaker: MS. CARTER
utterances.text: Certainly.

utterances.speaker: MS. CARTER
utterances.text: Sir, you've now indicated to the Court that portions of your unit did, in fact, become involved in direct combat operations. When did that occur?

utterances.speaker: PAVLE GAVRILOVIC
utterances.text: I did not say that they participated in direct combat operations. I have to repeat that once again or you misunderstood me.

utterances.speaker: MS. CARTER
utterances.text: Sir, I'm quoting from your answer. "In my statement, I already wrote and said that we directly took part -- we did not take part in any combat operations directly -- well, a few times we did, part of the unit, as I wrote in my statement. And in this case about 30 men who were used only to prevent spillovers of terrorists, or rather, to get them out of their positions."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Now, what is that other than saying we participated in a blockade?

utterances.speaker: MS. CARTER
utterances.text: Your Honours, according to this witness, that the blockade is that they never left that hilltop and that that is the only thing they were doing. (redacted)are much more in line with this description, that they did, in fact, go down and they were a part of removing the terrorists --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: That may be so, but you're accusing the witness of saying something different from what he said already, and I'm having difficulty identifying what the difference is.

utterances.speaker: MS. CARTER
utterances.text: Your Honour, I'm saying that --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: And that's the second objection taken to your cross-examination as being unfair to the witness, and that's a rather strong accusation to make. So can you point to me -- point out to me the contradiction you say that exists in this evidence?

utterances.speaker: MS. CARTER
utterances.text: Your Honour, this witness is clearly saying that there is a difference between direct involvement in combat operations and the indirect involvement. I'm trying to determine what was the direct -- when and if was there direct involvement, which is much more in line with what (redacted)--

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Where does he say so far that there was -- that his battalion was involved in direct combat operations? Where does he say that?

utterances.speaker: MS. CARTER
utterances.text: At page 79, beginning at line 1, there appears to be a differentiation. Mr. Ackerman then objected shortly thereafter, and I was not able to fully explore that --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: It says here clearly: "We did not take part in any combat operations directly," and then he goes on to explain that they did participate in a blockade.

utterances.speaker: MS. CARTER
utterances.text: It says "a few times," that does not isolate itself to one single incident, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: And you already have evidence from another witness today about much more direct involvement, but in any event if you wish to pursue this please do but based on appropriate questions and not unfair representations of what the witness has said or what the war diary says.

utterances.speaker: MS. CARTER
utterances.text: If Your Honour finds that there was better evidence given to today --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Not previous to today, we've had another witness dealing with the same area today.

utterances.speaker: MS. CARTER
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MS. CARTER
utterances.text: Sir, I would like to move on to P1981 in the English -- I'm sorry, in the B/C/S it's page 6, section G; and in the English it's page 8 in the first line, specifically drawing your attention to 8.7, subsection G calling for the logistical support. Sir, the witnesses (redacted)had indicated that after the operation took place that was referred to in P1995 that they were, in fact, involved in some sort of clean-up operation. However, in paragraph 13 of your statement you indicated that you never entered that village whatsoever but rather moved directly on to Prizren. What I'm trying to determine is if the order that was coming from your superior command indicates that you were to clear up the battle-field by engaging your own forces and equipment and once the combat group -- I'm sorry, once the combat operations are over in cooperation with organs in the territory. That seems consistent with their testimony. Are you telling me that every other member of the 549th was sent out to clean up this territory, but you however was not?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Mr. Bakrac.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, is my colleague suggesting that the entire 549th Brigade went to clear or clean up the battle-field? I don't see where it pertains to the logistics battalion. Where does it refer to the logistics battalion? This is an order of the commander of the entire 549th Brigade, and one cannot see who it is that is exactly involved in the clean-up.

utterances.speaker: MS. CARTER
utterances.text: Respectfully, Your Honour, if there is a combat operation taking place 500 metres from this unit - and there's been testimony from previous witnesses that they in fact were a part of that clean-up - I'm trying to determine how this witness can somehow disengage himself from that provision.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: This -- your question depends on an assumption that the order from his superior indicates that he was to clear up the battle-field. Now, where do we see that?

utterances.speaker: MS. CARTER
utterances.text: Your Honour, this goes to -- well, first off it's under logistical support is what begins 8.7 and the logistical support goes on -- talks about technical support, quarter-master support, medical support, it's going through, and it appears to give logistical tasks --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Yeah, but is it issued to the logistics battalion? It seems to be issued to Battle Groups 5, 6, 7, 1, and 2 of the 549th Motorised Brigade or am I misreading that?

utterances.speaker: MS. CARTER
utterances.text: That is what the receipt list indicates; however, this is the order that P1995, which is the combat report that we have been talking about quite exclusively in which this witness clearly says it is speaking about his unit and it placement.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: You should start this exercise again. Your question was really incomprehensible, Ms. Carter. You need to make this much simpler or much clearer, or it's going to be all wasted.

utterances.speaker: MS. CARTER
utterances.text: Certainly, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MS. CARTER
utterances.text: When the combat operations were over after the fourth day as described in P1995, what did your unit do?

utterances.speaker: PAVLE GAVRILOVIC
utterances.text: If you're referring to this concrete case that we were talking about, that we have talked about already, I wrote about that in my statement. I had nothing to do with combat operations. Once the task was completed, my unit withdrew to Prizren. We didn't do anything, no clean-up, no clearing up of the terrain, nothing.

utterances.speaker: MS. CARTER
utterances.text: If there was, in fact, an operation that took place 500 metres from you, who was then responsible for the clean-up of Trnje?

utterances.speaker: PAVLE GAVRILOVIC
utterances.text: I don't understand what clean-up of Trnje? I had a specific task and that's what I carried out. I did not receive any other tasks nor did I carry out any other tasks.

utterances.speaker: MS. CARTER
utterances.text: Sir, if there was a mopping-up operation that took place in Trnje, would you agree with me that that would have provided some deaths or some other destruction to Trnje village?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Don't answer that question. First of all, what is your basis for saying that there was a mopping-up operation in Trnje? Let's put that to the witness so that he's got the factual basis.

utterances.speaker: MS. CARTER
utterances.text: Certainly, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MS. CARTER
utterances.text: That would be P1995, the fourth day the last sentence that we've been exploring quite frequently in this case where it says that: "The STS had pulled out" --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Well, let's see it on the screen.

utterances.speaker: MS. CARTER
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated]

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Just a moment, Mr. Bakrac. Let us see.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It hasn't been announced, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Sorry, what has not been announced?

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The interpretation I got was document 1995.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: And there it is, hopefully.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It hadn't been part of a notice at all.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Let's enlarge the part that relates to the fourth day. It's the middle of the page, roughly. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Now, please proceed with your question.

utterances.speaker: MS. CARTER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. CARTER
utterances.text: Sir, I would direct you to the final sentence where it says: "The STS had pulled out into the villages of Trnje and Lesane during the night, they were routed and crushed" --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Well, you see, this is where we had a dispute about the translation, and the translation that Mr. Zecevic suggested was that they pulled out towards the villages of Trnje and Lesane after they had been routed and crushed, and we asked for a formal translation from CLSS. So I find it difficult to see how productive your questioning can be.

utterances.speaker: MS. CARTER
utterances.text: Respectfully, Your Honour, we're only dealing with a matter of metres. If we look at --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Oh, I agree -- I understand that, but where is the suggestion that Trnje was actually cleansed or mopped up or whatever the word is?

utterances.speaker: MS. CARTER
utterances.text: Respectfully, if you look at what occurred on the third day as well as what occurred on the fourth day, the third day it says: "The STS forces attempted to pull out along the creek to the villages of Trnje and Lesane," and then you look to that final sentence where it says they had pulled out. One says they were trying to and one says they did do that into the villages of Trnje and Lesane during the night, and they were also routed and crushed. So if you look at the two statements taken together, one is saying this was about to happen one said it did in fact happen, and they were routed and crushed. Thus, I believe that my questioning on this point is within the confines of P1995.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Well, your questioning depends on that being an accurate statement of what this document says.

utterances.speaker: MS. CARTER
utterances.text: Then in the event --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Which is in issue at the moment. But please proceed and see what answer you get.

utterances.speaker: MS. CARTER
utterances.text: Sir, if there appears to be some sort of routing and crushing, either directly in Trnje or just near Trnje, who would be the group responsible for cleaning up the battle-field?

utterances.speaker: PAVLE GAVRILOVIC
utterances.text: Well, I don't know in what sense you mean clean-up or mop-up of the terrain. I did not receive such an assignment. I did not carry out such an assignment; therefore, I don't know what group received such an assignment.

utterances.speaker: MS. CARTER
utterances.text: It's found in 8.7, logistical support, in the original order from the 549th. So if you are the logistics battalion yet you are not assigned to that type of support, what is the group that is?

utterances.speaker: PAVLE GAVRILOVIC
utterances.text: I don't understand, what group? What does this question refer to, what group?

utterances.speaker: MS. CARTER
utterances.text: We have heard evidence in this case from (redacted) that after the Trnje operation, they actually went down into Trnje and were cleaning up that area, and specifically that's where you get the testimony about the truck being seized at Hygijena and other items. What I am asking is that if they are, in fact, lying and they weren't any sort of any clear-up operation, who would be the group in this area that would have been responsible for that clean up?

utterances.speaker: PAVLE GAVRILOVIC
utterances.text: I don't know that, what group was responsible for any kind of clean up.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Mr. Gavrilovic, we constantly see in this courtroom orders directing a unit or other -- or units to clear up the battle-field, "asanacija" I think is the word that's used; is that a concept you're not familiar with?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, I have heard of that, but it's not that I got any task related to "asanacija," cleaning up the battle-field, or did I see any such thing ordered here.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: It tends to happen where there has been a battle and somebody has been routed and crushed, which seems to have happened here. Can you not help us with who had the task of clearing up at Trnje or in the area surrounding Trnje? You were only 500 metres away, after all.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, I don't know of anyone having the attack -- the task to carry out the clean up of that terrain.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Ms. Carter.

utterances.speaker: MS. CARTER
utterances.text: The final topic I'd like to speak with you about is in regards to some criminal reports and investigations that actually name you as a defendant. I want to pull up P982 at page 23 of the English and page 6 of the B/C/S, it's entry number 82.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Now, is he a defendant in current criminal proceedings?

utterances.speaker: MS. CARTER
utterances.text: This is what I'm trying to determine. It's blank in with regards to the final disposition on this.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Mr. Bakrac.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, if the number is correct, the P number mentioned in the transcript, 982, I don't have it on my list of exhibits for this witness.

utterances.speaker: MS. CARTER
utterances.text: And respectfully that is correct because it is 962, I apologise, it is the list of filed criminal reports against perpetrators in the 549th. I misspoke. It appears we have the correct page in the English and not in the B/C/S. It's going to be entry 82, it's page 6 of the B/C/S.

utterances.speaker: MS. CARTER
utterances.text: Sir, entry 82 lists actually a Major Pavle Gavrilovic of military post 4445/12. It does appear that this is a misidentification of your rank; however, that is your military post, is that correct, or was at the time?

utterances.speaker: PAVLE GAVRILOVIC
utterances.text: That's right. If it pertains to the year 2000, I was a major by then, or rather, 1999 too. I was a major already then too.

utterances.speaker: MS. CARTER
utterances.text: So the rank is correct. Now, according to this, you were charged under Article 174 for abuse of office. That is actually codified within the FRY criminal code which is at P1736. It indicates that you were being charged with abuse of office. Article 174 indicates that -- it's a charge against an official who by abusing his office or authority exceeding the limits of his official authority or failing to perform his official duties obtains a benefit for himself or another, causes damage to another, or seriously violates the rights of another. It goes on to give the punishment range. What occurred that you were being charged or being investigated under Article 174, abuse of office?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I don't know which specific case you're talking about. The only time I ever went to court, the only time I gave an affidavit in court - and it can't be anything else what you're talking about, there was just that one time that is categorised here or described as abuse of office and so on and so forth; so what was this about? During NATO aggression there was this van that was found in an area covered by my unit, a vehicle, a van. After that, some documents were drawn up that were necessary under the regulations, the documents that were required. So whether anyone thought they saw something or anybody reported theft that the van had been stolen or something like that, well the only thing that matter is in 1999 or 2000 I had to go to court back at our place, I showed my documents, the documents that I was in possession of, and the case was thrown out. I was never punished nor indeed had I ever done anything, and I committed absolutely no abuse of office.

utterances.speaker: MS. CARTER
utterances.text: Sir, why would you have been charged under the FRY code, which would be criminal offences against official duty by federal officials, as opposed to to being charged under the Serbian criminal code which tends to be where you find things such as theft, murder, and other common-law crimes. Why were you being charged under the FRY code?

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Mr. Bakrac, let the witness answer the question. You may have the explanation, but it's for him to deal with this.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I really don't know. I'm not even familiar with the provisions of this law. I'm not even sure that we're talking about the same thing because there was just this one time that I had to go to court about anything at all, and that's the time I told you about, and I have no idea about this criminal code or anything. I really don't know.

utterances.speaker: MS. CARTER
utterances.text: Okay. Now, you've said repeatedly that you've only been charged once and nothing ever occurred of it. I'd like to direct your attention to P3080, this is a report on the work of the judicial organs from 18 May 1999. In this, it indicates that you were actually -- a criminal report was filed against you in this case based on a violation of equality of citizens, which is what's codified under Article 186 of the FRY criminal code and specifically it reads that: "An official who on grounds of difference, nationality, race, religion, political or other beliefs, ethnicity, gender, language, education, or social position denies or restricts the rights of citizens laid down by the constitution, the law or any other regulation or general enactment or ratified international treaty or who on grounds of this difference grants citizens privileges or advantages." And it indicates that there shall be a punishment range. Sir, if this criminal report was filed against you, how is this involving a van and what took place when you were charged under 186?

utterances.speaker: PAVLE GAVRILOVIC
utterances.text: I don't know. I've never seen this before. No one has ever told me about anything like this, no one has ever accused me of anything. This is the first I see of it, and you're the first one to tell me about it.

utterances.speaker: MS. CARTER
utterances.text: So you --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CHOWHAN
utterances.text: Sorry I'm interrupting. I'm here, Witness. Please tell me you went to court, there must be a subpoena or a summons calling you to court, what were the allegations, were you charged, were you not charged, you have to tell us that. Because saying that you just walked into the court, it was not a courtesy call. They do not call people for a little explanation, this is the simple reaction where this may have happened; but this is a court calling you, so what really what happened? What was the charge?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CHOWHAN
utterances.text: We have not got reply even about the first one, this may not be true. But tell us, you admit that you have been once to the court, what was the charge? What happened? What the judge tell you, what you told the judge? What were the allegations, so we find out?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Perhaps I misphrased my first answer. I wasn't standing before a court in the sense of being tried. I had to go and see an investigating judge who was investigating certain allegations. The allegations that I explained, and then I came up with some documents which I showed to the investigating magistrate, and the case was thrown out, or rather, the investigation was terminated, whatever the correct expression is, it was dropped.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CHOWHAN
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. CARTER
utterances.text: Sir, I would now like to direct your attention to P3079, in subsection 2, that it indicated that: The military prosecutor's office submitted 28 requests for investigation to competent military courts, one of them was against you, this time we have a charge listed under 176 of the FRY Criminal Code. 176 is fraud in the discharge of office, specifically: "An official who in the discharge of his duties and with intent to obtain unlawful material benefit for himself or for another submits false statements of account or otherwise deceives an authorised person into making an unlawful disbursement," and then it gives the punishment ranges. Do you know anything about this investigation against you?

utterances.speaker: PAVLE GAVRILOVIC
utterances.text: I don't know about this investigation that was launched, but I see this is obviously the same thing that I have been talking about; it was about this van that was found in the deployment area of my unit. Someone or other may have reported a case of theft, I really don't know, but it can't possibly be in reference to anything else simply because I'm totally clueless about any other reports or investigations or anything like that.

utterances.speaker: MS. CARTER
utterances.text: Okay. So this one may or may not be what you're talking about; however, you have no indication about any charges that were levied against you under Article 174, abuse of office or power, or under 186 violation of equality of citizens. You have no knowledge of either of these two charges?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Well, he does. He's told you -- he's dealt with the 174 and he has no knowledge of the 186, as I understand it.

utterances.speaker: MS. CARTER
utterances.text: Your Honour, there's three, 174 is listed in P982 --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Yes, that's the -- 962 is the correct number.

utterances.speaker: MS. CARTER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: And that's the one where he was charged with abuse of office, it was investigated by an investigating judge, he produced the records according to him, and that was it. Have I misunderstood that?

utterances.speaker: MS. CARTER
utterances.text: Your Honour, there are two separate articles. He's indicated that that is this van as well as the charge under 176, which is 3079, that that --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: All he's saying is he thinks it may be the same.

utterances.speaker: MS. CARTER
utterances.text: Your Honour, this is two completely different criminal codes. I'm trying to determine which if any of these is the van and what explanation if any he has for the other two.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: But one is -- one is an abuse of office, the other is fraud in discharge of office, and he says he's only been involved in a court investigation on one occasion. So what more do you expect to get from him?

utterances.speaker: MS. CARTER
utterances.text: Your Honour, given that we have heard much evidence about the functioning of the military courts, how once these reports get filed they were properly investigated, they went to an investigative judge, et cetera, et cetera, it appears that this witness is contradicting what that procedure actually took place on the ground. So I want to develop that a little bit further. Obviously this witness -- he's indicating that he's only aware of one charge, yet we have documents from the military that he, in fact, has been charged under three separate codes and most concerning of all is the violation of equality of citizens. I'm not clear how that has anything to do with the matter.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Ms. Carter, two of your documents are requests for investigation and no more than that, and the one which goes further he has dealt with. Now, you're perfectly entitled to pursue these, but please don't misrepresent what you've got in front of you.

utterances.speaker: MS. CARTER
utterances.text: Your Honour, one is actually a request for investigation one is a criminal report --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Which one is the criminal report?

utterances.speaker: MS. CARTER
utterances.text: The criminal report is P3080. It says: "The military prosecutor's office received 59 criminal reports for processing," and it enumerates these.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: All right. My apologies, but that's a criminal report and that's as far as you seem to have got it at the moment. However, please continue with appropriate questions.

utterances.speaker: MS. CARTER
utterances.text: Sir, when a complaint is levied against an officer within the VJ, is it commonplace for the person to at minimum be questioned about the criminal report?

utterances.speaker: PAVLE GAVRILOVIC
utterances.text: Of course, yes. Or at least I think so.

utterances.speaker: MS. CARTER
utterances.text: All right. Yet in this case you said you were only questioned once. Can you tell me what time-period you were actually being questioned or what the approximate date of the offence was?

utterances.speaker: PAVLE GAVRILOVIC
utterances.text: I really can't remember when that was, but I do know that it was -- I don't know. Certainly -- I can't remember the exact date. I know that I did see an investigating judge. I made a statement, I showed him the documents about that van, what I told you about before, and that was the only and that is the only report that I am aware of nor did anyone question me on any other occasion. I don't think charges were pressed ever because I never faced a court.

utterances.speaker: MS. CARTER
utterances.text: Are you at least given notice that -- when charges -- or when a complaint is filed against you?

utterances.speaker: PAVLE GAVRILOVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. CARTER
utterances.text: As it appears that this witness can't enlighten us any further as regards the work of the legal affairs organ, I pass the witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Thank you, Ms. Carter. Mr. Bakrac, and can you tell us whether we can go into open session or not.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honour, I believe we can. I have a single question about a particular document.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We are in open session, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Gavrilovic, a single question for you.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we please have Exhibit P1981. [Trial Chamber and registrar confer].

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Mr. Bakrac, this exhibit is under seal, so we will not --

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I do apologise.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Well, we can still have the evidence in open session, but the exhibit will not be published beyond the courtroom.
